title: Living rubber stamp
technique: Stamped phrases feed a reaction-diffusion simulation, so the letters grow coral-like tendrils and beads.
music: Each kick drum presses the letters solid again, and between kicks they hollow into outlines, worms and beads; a new song section brings a new phrase and ink. Louder, bassier passages let the growth spread further from the letters, snares burn it back, and high hits make the ink glint.
as_processor: Stamps the bright shapes of the picture into the simulation in place of the words, so its outlines stand up as gold, enamel or tar ink that follows the picture as it moves and grows and breaks up between kick drums; two takes also print the picture itself on the page underneath.
words_with_input: The bright shapes of another picture are the stamp. Each kick drum presses them again.

takes.name: Desk
takes.description: A tilted cream star chart with one framed phrase stamped on it, seen wide and then slowly closing in, with the ink changing between gold, red and black by song section.
words: Two simulated chemicals on a 640 x 360 grid. One feeds on the other, and both spread.
1 The stamped letters are poured in as chemical.
2 It grows outward from them as worms, beads and coral.
3 Each kick drum presses the letters solid again.
4 Snare hits burn the growth back.
5 Louder, bassier music lets it spread further.
Gray-Scott model, 10 steps per frame, in a GLSL shader. The pattern is lit as a height map.
Stamped letters seed a Gray-Scott simulation. Each kick drum presses them solid again.

takes.name: Macro
takes.description: The same paper from a few centimetres up with shallow focus, so the edge of the ink becomes a landscape and no word can be read.
words: THE INK IS A HEIGHT MAP

takes.name: Field
takes.description: No page at all: seen from above, the whole frame is twelve short words dissolving into worms, in dithered pure black and white.
words: Short words dissolve into worms and spots, in 1-bit dither. Kick drums re-ink about half.

takes.name: Approvals
takes.description: A blueprint seen from straight above with six small crooked stamps in gold, red and black, and each kick presses about a third of them again.
words: Every stamp is a seed for the same reaction-diffusion simulation.
Gold leaf, red enamel and black tar are three ways of lighting one pattern.
Each kick drum presses about a third of the stamps again.
Snare hits burn the growth back. Hi-hats make the ink glint.
Louder, bassier music lets the ink creep further from the letters.
Six stamps in three inks, all one simulation. Each kick drum presses a third of them again.

takes.name: Carbon
takes.description: A negative version with white ink on dark carbon paper, where an oversized unframed phrase is seen from one end like road markings, in shallow focus.
words: The same simulation as white ink on dark carbon paper, seen from one end of the phrase.

takes.name: Ticket
takes.description: A pink admission ticket from above, where one small black stamp lands somewhere new on every kick and leaves its red impressions behind.
words: Every kick drum lands a new stamp in a new place.
The black ink is a reaction-diffusion simulation:
it keeps growing and breaking up after it lands.
The red marks are where earlier stamps were pressed.
Gray-Scott model on a 640 x 360 grid, 10 steps per frame.
Every kick drum lands a new stamp. The black ink keeps growing; red marks are old stamps.

takes.name: Relic
takes.description: No paper: the same living ink is wrapped around a 3D object (an amphora, a pierced stone sculpture or a space helmet) turning in the dark.
words: The same living ink projected onto a 3D model from three sides. Kick drums re-ink it.
